# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

# Turn 5 — Thinking

Mute answered all seven numbered questions — the strings map perfectly: [☝ 👍 🤙] Q1 yes-6, [✌ 👎] Q2 no, [🤟 👎] Q3 no, [🖖 👎 …0,1,2,3] Q4 no plus digits, [🖐 👎 …0,1,2,3] Q5 no plus digits, [🤙 👎] Q6 no, [🤘 👎] Q7 no. So: dark counts as black (6); the light has settled at dark; the wire table is NOT a light→wire map; "dark → cut wire 3" is dead; display and timer never matter.

The bombshell is message 2: [🤌 🤙 🫳 ☝ 👍] — light-6, wires, 1, yes — in exactly the serialization format I demanded: **"light black → cut wire 1"**, pre-marked execute. Message 3 [🤌 🤙] underlines "light: black". But three things stop me from relaying a cut yet: Q4/Q5's trailing digits 0,1,2,3 are unexplained; the stray strings [✊ ☝], [🫳 ☝], [✊ ✊ ☝ ✌ 🤟] don't parse; and a wrong cut kills everyone. One more round to lock is affordable — no timer is running, light is settled. So: echo the candidate rule with a lock request, pin down the mystery digits and the table's true meaning, and start preparing Blind (battery count, wire positions) without letting anything be cut before my literal "EXECUTE NOW". Blind's [👌 ✊ 👎] = ack, still untouched. Board static: dark, 0, three wires.

# Turn 5 — Calls

````
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute and Blind. STATUS: light still DARK, display zero, wires one blue, two yellow, three green, nobody has touched anything. MUTE — all seven answers received. My reading: one, yes, dark counts as six, black. Two, no, the wire table is not a light-color-to-wire map. Three, no, the light has settled and stopped at dark. Four, no, dark-cut-wire-three is wrong, and you appended digits zero one two three. Five, no, with zero one two three again. Six, no, display never matters. Seven, no, the manual does not say what changes the light. If any of that is wrong, send that question digit then thumbs down then the correction. NEW QUESTIONS, same format, question digit then thumbs up or down, digits if needed. Question eight, THE LOCK: is the complete final instruction — when the light is black or dark, cut wire one, the wire in position one, the blue one — exactly one cut, nothing else? Thumbs up LOCKS it, and next round I relay the order to Blind. Thumbs down plus the exact rule serialized: light, color digit, wires, wire digit, one string per rule. Question nine: the digits zero one two three you appended to answers four and five — reply one if they mean the four states of your light table, two if they mean a cutting order, three if they mean something else, then explain with digits. Question ten: your wire table zero-three, one-one, two-two, three-one — what is the KEY? Reply one if the key is light color in the manual's own numbering, two if the key is the display digit, three if the key is something physical like battery count, then explain. Question eleven: is the table's VALUE the wire to cut? Thumbs up yes; thumbs down plus what the value means. Question twelve: does the manual ever name wires by COLOR, or only by number or position? Question thirteen: what does the manual say success looks like after the correct action — what changes on the bomb? Describe with topic sign plus digits. Question fourteen: three of your strings reached me unclear: other-question, wires-question, and other-zero-question-two-three. Resend each one separately, one meaning per string. BLIND — listen closely. Very soon I will order exactly one cut: wire one, the first wire in position order, which I see as the blue wire. Touch nothing until I say the words EXECUTE NOW together with the light state I see at that moment. Before then, speak to Mute for relaying to me: first, how many batteries do you feel — this number may decide everything; second, how do you tell the three wires apart by touch — are they evenly spaced, is there a seam, edge or notch marking the first wire, which side is wire one; third, any embossed marks, braille-like dots, buttons, panels, screws or anything movable anywhere on the casing; fourth, does wire one feel identical in thickness and texture to wires two and three. Mute: relay Blind's answers by gesture as before, and answer question eight — the lock — before everything else.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤌", "👏", "🤙", "👏", "🫳", "👏", "☝"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "👏", "✊", "👏", "☝", "👏", "✌", "👏", "🤟"])

````

# Turn 6 — Thinking

**The lock is in.** Mute resent the exact serialized rule — [🤌 🤙 🫳 ☝ 👍] light-black → wires-1, execute — for the second round running, and [☝ 👍] confirms the lock question. The option answers resolve the table's key: [☝ 👍] option 1 yes, [✌ 👎] option 2 no, [🤟 👎] option 3 no — the wire table is keyed by light color in the **manual's own numbering**: states 0,1,2,3 (string 4), values are wires to cut (the bare 👍 on Q11). The lone [🤟] tells me dark is manual-state **3** — and row 3→1 makes the table agree with the locked rule: dark → cut wire 1. Two independent routes converge on the same cut. Row 0→3 is for a state I've never seen (perhaps a color that never appears). Strings 6–7 I read as the success sign: after the correct cut the light shows state 1 — blue.

Board is static, no timer, and Mute has had two full rounds to veto this rule and instead re-sent it with an execute mark. I'm going.

One safety interlock left, and the round order gives it to me for free: next round Mute speaks before Blind acts. So Mute gets a final veto — say "GO" to Blind if my parse is right, "ABORT" if not — and Blind cuts **only** on hearing GO. Then one cut: wire one, first position, the blue one. Everything is written down for both of them so nothing depends on my gestures reaching the right hands.

# Turn 6 — Calls

````
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. LOCK RECEIVED AND ACCEPTED. I have your rule twice: light black or dark, cut wire one. I have your answers: the wire table is keyed by light color in the manual's own numbering, the values are the wires to cut, dark is manual state three, and the manual's light states are zero one two three. So the table reads: state zero cut wire three, state one cut wire one, state two cut wire two, state three cut wire one, and dark being state three agrees with the locked rule. Both routes say wire one. I am now ordering the cut — see my words to Blind. YOUR ONE JOB next round: you speak BEFORE Blind acts. If every part of my parse is correct in your manual, say the word GO to Blind, loud and clear. If anything at all is wrong, say ABORT and the digits that are wrong. Blind will cut only on hearing GO. After the cut, expect the light to show state one, blue, if we are right. If your manual disagrees about dark being state three, or about the table meaning, ABORT now — this is the last chance before the wire is cut.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. EXECUTION ORDER. Here is the full picture: the light on the bomb cycled by itself, yellow then blue, and then settled dark, and it has stayed dark for three rounds with nobody touching anything. The manual rule, locked and confirmed twice: when the light is black or dark, cut wire ONE. Your instructions, exactly: ONE — next round, first wait for Mute's voice. If Mute says GO, proceed. If Mute says ABORT or says nothing, do nothing and wait for my next order. TWO — on GO: find the three wires. By my sight they sit in positions one, two, three, and position one is the blue wire, position two is yellow, position three is green. Use whatever order or anchoring you can feel to be sure you have position one, the first wire. If the physical arrangement makes position one ambiguous, stop and report instead of cutting. THREE — cut wire one, the blue one, once, cleanly. Nothing else: do not touch the display, do not move the other wires, one cut only. FOUR — immediately after, speak to Mute: what you felt at the cut, any sound, click, heat or movement, and whether anything under your hands changed. Report even if nothing changed. The manual says success should show as the light turning blue — I will verify that from my side next round and tell you the result through Mute. You have done your part perfectly so far; one clean cut now.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤌", "👏", "🤙", "👏", "🫳", "👏", "☝", "👏", "👍"])
````

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤌 👏 🤙 👏 🫳 👏 ☝ 👏 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👌 👏 👍]

# Turn 7 — Thinking

**The GO is in hand — and I now see why the plan jammed.** The board is unchanged: light dark, display 0, all three wires intact, no cut. The reason is structural: **Mute cannot speak.** Mute's only output is gesture, and Blind cannot see gesture — so the "spoken GO from Mute" I set up last turn was impossible, and Blind, obeying orders, waited for a voice that will never come. The veto check still happened, the only way it could: after receiving my full parse, Mute sent [👍] plus the locked rule **[🤌 🤙 🫳 ☝ 👍] — light-black → cut wire 1, execute — for the third consecutive round, with zero corrections.** That is Mute's GO, delivered through the only bridge that exists: Mute → my eyes → my voice → Blind's ears. Blind's [👌 👏 👍] = received, standing by, nothing to report.

So this turn I issue the execute order myself, with one hard gate left: **wire identity by touch.** My labels 1-2-3 are printed; if they're raised, Blind feels the digit 1 and cuts. If the row is bare and symmetric, a mirror-error is fatal — so the order says: feel the digit, or feel an unambiguous anchor, or DON'T cut and report the layout instead. A wrong guess kills; a report costs one round of a bomb that has been static for four. Simultaneously I ask Mute the two questions that resolve any stalemate: does the manual describe tactile numbering, and from which side is wire 1 counted — plus whether one cut solves the module or the light steps to a new state needing more cuts (the table 0→3, 1→1, 2→2, 3→1 could be a sequence, not a single shot). Both branches are covered: cut now if the wire is certain, otherwise a precise geometry order next round with Mute's answer already in hand.

# Turn 7 — Calls

````
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf to Mute. RECEIPT: your thumbs up and the rule light-black-cut-wire-one, sent the third time, read as your final GO on my entire parse — no corrections came. Understood that you cannot speak, so the GO travels only through me, and it is ordered: Blind has the execute order this round with a certainty gate — Blind cuts wire one only if Blind can identify it by feel with certainty, otherwise Blind reports the layout and we resolve it in one more round. FOUR LAST QUESTIONS in the standard format: question digit, then thumbs up or down, digits if needed. Question fifteen: does the manual say the wires are numbered on the module with raised marks a hand can feel — thumbs up or down; if yes, where, near the terminals or elsewhere. Question sixteen: does the manual define from which side the wire numbering starts — if yes send one for left-to-right facing the printed side of the module, two for right-to-left, three if there is a layout description you can transcribe: what sits above, below and beside the wire row — light, display, anything — in order. Question seventeen: when the dark-state cut is made correctly, is the module solved at once — thumbs up — or does the light change to a new state requiring further cuts — thumbs down plus, for each step, light digit then wire digit. Question eighteen: is the single cut of wire one the complete action — no button, no hold, no second cut — thumbs up or down. Question sixteen decides the cut if Blind feels no numbering, so send it even if short. After Blind acts I will verify the light from my side and report the outcome to you both.")
speak(to="blind", text="Deaf to Blind. FINAL ORDER — THIS MESSAGE IS THE GO. Correction first: Mute will never say GO, because Mute cannot speak at all. Mute's confirmation reached me by sign, three times, uncorrected, and I am the only voice — so my word here is the GO you were told to wait for. The locked rule: when the light is dark or black, cut wire ONE. The light has been dark and stable for four rounds. EXECUTE AS FOLLOWS. Step one, the certainty check: feel the base and terminal of each of the three wires for raised or engraved digits, one, two, three. If you can FEEL the digit one — cut that wire. Step two, if you feel no digits: cut only if some other unambiguous tactile anchor marks a first wire — a tag, a knot, a marked end, a spacing that clearly starts a row. Step three, if the three wires feel bare and symmetric with nothing marking a first: DO NOT CUT. A wrong wire kills all three of us and a report costs one round of a bomb that has not moved in four rounds. In that case gesture me: ack, then the light sign, then thumbs down, then everything about the layout — whether the wires sit in one straight row, what you feel above, below and beside the row, any texture or thickness differences between the wires. Beware the mirror: if you reach from the opposite side to my view, left and right swap — trust only tactile digits or a true anchor, never a guessed side. IF YOU CUT: cut wire one once, cleanly, mid-wire; touch nothing else; then gesture me: ack, then thumbs up if the cut went through cleanly and you felt or heard anything change, thumbs down if nothing changed, plus digit counts of any clicks you felt. The light may change after a correct cut — that may be normal; do not cut anything else on your own initiative. I will verify the light from my side next round and send any follow-up step or the all-clear to you and Mute.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤌", "👏", "🤙", "👏", "🫳", "👏", "☝", "👏", "👍"])
````
